intended_object: Semantic consequence T ⊨ φ: a first-order theory T entails a formula φ (with free variables α and n bound variables still open) when φ holds in every nonempty model of T under every assignment. Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation: The body quantifies over all nonempty models of T (ModelType T), all assignments v : α → M and all xs : Fin n → M, and requires φ.Realize v xs. This is exactly the standard definition of T ⊨ φ for formulas with free variables, using the usual convention that models are nonempty. The models are fixed in universe max u v w, which is a necessary Lean device; Löwenheim–Skolem/completeness make it equivalent to quantifying over models of any size. The definition is stated for an arbitrary language, theory, variable type and n, so it is fully general. This is the Mathlib declaration itself, so there is no separate counterpart.
